ABOUT THE CENTER

Rooted in life science
Connecting research with application

Bringing disciplines together to address real needs.
Turning life science innovation into applications for health.

Based in the School of Life Sciences at Southern University of Science and Technology, the Innovative Center for Life Science and Health (ICLH) draws on strengths in structural biology, neuroscience and synthetic biology. It brings technology translation, academic exchange and interdisciplinary education together in one platform.

Responding to innovation priorities in the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area and the needs of Shenzhen’s biomedical and health industries, the center connects university research with industry practice across research, education and application.

PARTNERSHIPS & EDUCATION

Advancing innovation through partnership

Strategic partnerships

Connecting clinical resources with engineering expertise to explore new health applications.

Child health · Clinical collaboration

Chongqing Xiaomixiong Children’s Hospital Co., Ltd.

This partnership focuses on health throughout childhood. Planned collaboration will combine university research expertise with clinical resources to study brain development, interventions for brain disorders and cognitive health in children.

Medical engineering · Emergency response

Shenzhen Rongyi Electronic Technology Co., Ltd.

The collaboration explores public health emergency response, outdoor rescue and population health monitoring, drawing on low-altitude monitoring, remote inspection, emergency delivery and intelligent data collection.

ENTREPRENEURSHIP EDUCATION

INTERDISCIPLINARY PROJECTS

Across disciplines
Exploring new possibilities for health

01 / Emergency response

Life sciences × Intelligent emergency response

Ruiying Emergency Eye

The project brings people, aerial systems and ground vehicles together in a coordinated emergency response network, exploring ways to improve prehospital care for cardiac arrest and other emergencies.

It addresses the critical first four minutes of cardiac arrest response and seeks to close gaps in complex rescue settings, providing technical support for public emergency services.

Explore the research ＋

An integrated air–ground network connects on-site response with emergency command, linking technology development to practical rescue needs.

02 / Synthetic biology

Life sciences × Computational design

Environmentally Robust
LLPS Scaffold Protein
Design and Optimization

The project explores principles for designing condensates that remain robust across cell types, variations in expression and environmental perturbations.

Potential applications include artificial membraneless organelles, pathway compartmentalization, signaling regulation, cell factories and therapeutic cell engineering.

Explore the research ＋

LLPS stands for liquid–liquid phase separation. The research studies how scaffold protein combinations perform across environments and explores more adaptable design strategies.

03 / Drug discovery

Life sciences × Artificial intelligence

AI-Driven
RNA Drug Discovery

Research teams led by Professors Wei Chen and Zefeng Wang at SUSTech School of Life Sciences are exploring an AI-driven platform for RNA drug discovery.

The platform uses large AI models for RNA sequence optimization, molecular screening and delivery system design, linking target discovery, molecular design, lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery optimization and preclinical validation.

Explore the research ＋

Combining computational approaches with experimental research, the project explores ways to improve molecular design and delivery optimization throughout the RNA drug discovery process.
